slides.title: Designing well-conditioned workspaces (Manipulability)

visualInspection.notes: Task singularity is Jacobian rank loss. det(J)=0 applies to square J. Manipulability is √det(JJᵀ), reducing to |det J| for square J. Conditioning and directional uniformity are not fully described by the determinant product alone. Viewed actual readable 1800×1013 source pixels alongside extracted text.

slides.title: Inertia Ellipsoid :

visualInspection.notes: The inertia discussion attributed to Asada uses M_x=J^(−T)MJ^(−1), requiring square nonsingular J. The normalized quadratic form XᵀM_xX=1 gives an inertia metric ellipsoid. Equal principal values give isotropy. The figure displays changing local ellipse shapes and directions, not prescribed trajectories or universal actuator-limited acceleration bounds.
